title: Streaming flow-control: handle client disconnects, timeouts, and partial-generation cleanup
creator: Ava Reynolds
description: When clients stream completions we currently rely on best-effort TCP/HTTP semantics to terminate work. This ticket scopes work to implement robust flow-control and cleanup for streaming inference: detect client disconnects and cancelled requests rapidly, apply graceful partial-generation cleanup (KV cache and memory), enforce server-side timeouts, and provide deterministic observable signals to clients and the Console. Goals: 1) reduce wasted GPU cycles from orphaned streams; 2) ensure deterministic resource reclamation within bounded time; 3) make failure modes visible to customers (clear error types and metrics); 4) provide SDK-level ergonomics for mid-stream cancellation/backoff. This includes protocol-level behavior, runtime changes in the serving layer, updates to SDKs (node/python), and Console/alerting integration.
acceptance_criteria: Server detects client TCP/HTTP disconnects within 3s and cancels corresponding in-flight generation
Server-side per-request streaming timeout (configurable) enforced and observable via tracing and metrics
KV cache entries and ephemeral buffers reclaimed deterministically within 10s of cancellation
SDKs expose a standardized stream.cancel() and map server disconnects to a cancel/error callback
E2E tests that simulate disconnects/timeouts pass in CI across cpu/gpu variants
Console surfaces a new stream_disconnects metric and per-route breakdown
comments: 2026-03-10 - Ava Reynolds: Initial triage. Observed increased GPU time spent on orphaned streams during ramp tests. Prior attempts (ENG-4799) added coarse timeouts but did not handle mid-stream client aborts.
2026-03-11 - Marcus Chen: Design proposal posted in Confluence (link in attachments). Proposing a layered approach: transport watcher -> request lease -> async cancel token -> reclamation job.
2026-03-12 - Priya Kapoor (PM): Customer impacted for long-running streaming demos; requested high signal fidelity in Console and a short-term mitigation toggle for Dedicated customers.

2026-03-13 - Marcus Chen: Implemented transport watcher prototype, added unit tests for cancel token propagation. Observed clean cancellation in local harness. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1123 (draft).

rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag 'streaming.cleanup.v1' (off in prod by default)
Canary on dedicated-only region cluster (canary size: 5% traffic) for 48h
Monitor key metrics (see monitoring_metrics); if >2x baseline cancel latency, rollback
Gradual ramp to 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 7 days with follow-up performance validation
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Aggressive cancellation could drop legitimately slow clients. Mitigation: configurable grace period per route and SDK-level acknowledgement of soft-cancel.
Risk: Reclamation penalties might cause GC spikes on busy nodes. Mitigation: background reclamation with rate limit and backpressure-exempt path for critical control-plane flows.
Risk: Back-compat with older SDKs. Mitigation: compatibility layer will map unknown disconnect signals to conservative server-side timeouts for 3 months, then deprecate.
Risk: Observability gaps. Mitigation: add debug tracing spans on cancel/callback and an aggregated metric and dashboard before rollout.
test_plan: Unit tests for cancel-token propagation through request pipeline
Integration tests simulating: mid-stream client TCP close, HTTP RESET, SDK cancel() call, and connection flaps
Load test: measure wasted GPU time during simulated 1% disconnect rate across 1M tokens/hour workload
Chaos run: random network partitions in staging with reclamation enabled
SDK tests to validate stream.cancel() semantics and error mapping
monitoring_metrics: stream_disconnects.count - total stream disconnect events per minute
stream_cancel_latency.p95 - time between detection and runtime cancellation
orphaned_gpu_seconds - GPU seconds consumed by streams flagged as orphaned
kv_reclaim_latency.p95 - time to evict ephemeral KV cache entries after cancel
stream_errors.client_disconnect - distinct error code surfaced to clients
